claim: The attachment site of the rotator cuff (RC) is a classic fibrocartilaginous enthesis, which is the junction between bone and tendon with typical characteristics of a fibrocartilage transition zone.
source: The attachment site of the rotator cuff (RC) is a classic fibrocartilaginous enthesis, which is the junction between bone and tendon with typical characteristics of a fibrocartilage transition zone.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a definitional claim about the RC attachment site.

claim: RC and its enthesis are essential components of the shoulder, which are critical in facilitating coordinated shoulder movements and stability.
source: RC and its enthesis are essential components of the shoulder, which are critical in facilitating coordinated shoulder movements and stability (Schett et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schett et al., 2017.

claim: The attachment site of supraspinatus (SS) tendon is vulnerable to injury and difficult to achieve complete regeneration, due to its high heterogeneity in composition and structure.
source: Compared to other RC tissues, the attachment site of supraspinatus (SS) tendon is vulnerable to injury and difficult to achieve complete regeneration, due to its high heterogeneity in composition and structure (Nourissat et al., 2015; Schett et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nourissat et al., 2015 and Schett et al., 2017.

claim: The attachment site of the SS tendon is a classic fibrocartilaginous enthesis, also termed BTJ.
source: Histologically, the attachment site of the SS tendon is a classic fibrocartilaginous enthesis, also termed BTJ (Chen et al., 2021a; Rossetti et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2021a and Rossetti et al., 2017.

claim: The fibrocartilaginous enthesis exhibits gradations in tissue organization, cell phenotype, and matrix composition in its native state.
source: In its native state, the fibrocartilaginous enthesis exhibits gradations in tissue organization, cell phenotype, and matrix composition (Moffat et al., 2008; Rossetti et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Moffat et al., 2008 and Rossetti et al., 2017.

claim: Fibrocartilaginous entheses manage to disperse stress and facilitate load transfer between vastly different materials like tendons and bone, with modulus ranging from 200 MPa to 20 GPa.
source: Fibrocartilaginous entheses manage to disperse stress and facilitate load transfer between vastly different materials like tendons and bone, with modulus ranging from 200 MPa to 20 GPa (Rossetti et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rossetti et al., 2017 and includes specific quantitative data about modulus range.

claim: The intrinsic regenerative capacity of fibrocartilaginous enthesis is not well-understood.
source: Unfortunately, the intrinsic regenerative capacity of fibrocartilaginous enthesis is not well-understood, which limits the exploitation of the best and most rigorously proven early intervention programs (Derwin et al., 2018; Schett et al., 2017; Xiao et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Derwin et al., 2018, Schett et al., 2017, and Xiao et al., 2022.

claim: The fibrocartilage layer is formed by a pool of site-specific progenitor cells, and initially organizes as an unmineralized cartilaginous attachment unit.
source: Details are scarce, but the fibrocartilage layer is formed by a pool of site-specific progenitor cells, and initially organizes as an unmineralized cartilaginous attachment unit (Jensen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jensen et al., 2018.

claim: The development pattern of enthesis fibrocartilage shares an overlapping biological behavior with the growth plate, which is a process of mesenchymal stem cells differentiating into chondrogenic cells and then sequentially into fibrocartilage cells.
source: Such development pattern shares an overlapping biological behavior with the growth plate, which is a process of mesenchymal stem cells differentiating into chondrogenic cells and then sequentially into fibrocartilage cells (Killian, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Killian, 2022.

claim: A unique enthesis progenitor pool has been identified since the embryonic stages, as cells sandwiched between primary cartilage and tendon, expressing a mixed transcriptome of both chondrogenic and tenogenic genomic features (Scleraxis and SRY-related transcription factor).
source: A unique enthesis progenitor pool has been identified since the embryonic stages, as cells sandwiched between primary cartilage and tendon, expressing a mixed transcriptome of both chondrogenic and tenogenic genomic features (Scleraxis and SRY-related transcription factor) (Blitz et al., 2013; Sugimoto et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Blitz et al., 2013 and Sugimoto et al., 2013.

claim: Enthesis progenitors can differentiate into either chondrocytes or tendon fibroblasts, under the regulation of Krüppel-like (Klf) transcription factors.
source: These enthesis progenitors can differentiate into either chondrocytes or tendon fibroblasts, under the regulation of Krüppel-like (Klf) transcription factors (Kult et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kult et al., 2021.

claim: In the later embryonic and postnatal stages, cells from the enthesis progenitor pool ultimately either differentiate into or are replaced by a Hh-positive cell population marked by Gli1 and Ptch1.
source: In the later embryonic and postnatal stages, cells from the enthesis progenitor pool ultimately either differentiate into or are replaced by a Hh-positive cell population marked by Gli1 and Ptch1 (Felsenthal et al., 2018; Schwartz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Felsenthal et al., 2018 and Schwartz et al., 2015.

claim: Gli1+ cells and their progenies are retained in the enthesis region throughout postnatal development and eventually populate the entire fibrocartilage region between tendon and bone, thereby contributing to enthesis growth.
source: Gli1+ cells and their progenies are retained in the enthesis region throughout postnatal development and eventually populate the entire fibrocartilage region between tendon and bone, thereby contributing to enthesis growth (Felsenthal et al., 2018; Jensen et al., 2018; Schwartz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Felsenthal et al., 2018, Jensen et al., 2018, and Schwartz et al., 2015.

claim: The normal enthesis maintains a gradient of cell phenotypes, from tendon fibroblast to chondrocyte then to mineralizing chondrocyte and to osteoblast/osteocyte.
source: As is proved, the normal enthesis maintains a gradient of cell phenotypes, from tendon fibroblast to chondrocyte then to mineralizing chondrocyte and to osteoblast/osteocyte (Chen et al., 2021b; Moffat et al., 2008; Rossetti et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2021b, Moffat et al., 2008, and Rossetti et al., 2017.

claim: scRNA-seq is a powerful method to analyze various cell types and provide insights into tendon enthesis postnatal development.
source: scRNA-seq is a powerful method to analyze various cell types and provide insights into tendon enthesis postnatal development (Gulati et al., 2020; Kult et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gulati et al., 2020 and Kult et al., 2021.

claim: Fang Fei et al. reported an exciting single-cell work to define the enthesis cell transcriptomes at postnatal day 11, 18, and 56, revealed the clonogenicity and multipotency of enthesis Gli1+ progenitors.
source: Recently, Fang Fei et al., reported an exciting single-cell work to define the enthesis cell transcriptomes at postnatal day 11, 18, and 56, revealed the clonogenicity and multipotency of enthesis Gli1+ progenitors (Fang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fang et al., 2022.

claim: At postnatal day 1, an articular cavity was formed and the supraspinatus tendon (ST) was observed attached to the humeral head.
source: At postnatal day 1, an articular cavity was formed and the supraspinatus tendon (ST) was observed attached to the humeral head.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological images in Figure 1a showing P1 samples.

claim: The cells at the ST attachment site were highly dense and homogeneous at postnatal day 1, and were visibly different from tendon cells and the primary cartilage cells inside the humeral head.
source: The cells at the ST attachment site were highly dense and homogeneous, and were visibly different from tendon cells and the primary cartilage cells inside the humeral head, suggesting that postnatal enthesis is formed by site-specific progenitor cells since the embryonic stage.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological observations in Figure 1a.

claim: At P1, P3, and P7, the fibrocartilage layer and subchondral bone could hardly be visualized.
source: At P1, P3, and P7, the fibrocartilage layer and subchondral bone could hardly be visualized.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological images in Figure 1a.

claim: Fibrocartilage was not evident at the enthesis of the mouse rotator cuff until 2–3 weeks after birth.
source: Fibrocartilage was not evident at the enthesis of the mouse rotator cuff until 2–3 weeks after birth.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological observations in Figure 1a showing developmental progression.

claim: Cell size remarkably increased during postnatal development, from postnatal day 7–14.
source: To examine the cellular morphological changes, we further measured the 2D parameters (including 2D area, roundness, frete diameter, and minimal frete diameter) of enthesis cells, statistics results demonstrated that cell size remarkably increased during postnatal development, from postnatal day 7–14 (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1d.

claim: After postnatal day 14, the enthesis cells were observed as typical chondrocyte phenotype, column-like stacked alongside the direction of tendon fiber, with more prominent patterns at P28 and P56.
source: After postnatal day 14, the enthesis cells were observed as typical chondrocyte phenotype, column-like stacked alongside the direction of tendon fiber, with more prominent patterns at P28 and P56.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological observations in Figure 1a.

claim: Fibrochondrocytes can be observed since P14, with a larger cellular size in comparison with condensed primary chondrocytes in P7.
source: From toluidine blue/fast green stainings, fibrochondrocytes can be observed since P14, with a larger cellular size in comparison with condensed primary chondrocytes in P7.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by toluidine blue/fast green staining images in Figure 1a.

claim: The extracellular matrix (ECM) of fibrocartilage with mineralization can be observed after P28.
source: The extracellular matrix (ECM) of fibrocartilage with mineralization can be observed after P28.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by histological observations in Figure 1a.

claim: Type 2 collagen is a major ECM component of cartilage.
source: Type 2 collagen is a major ECM component of cartilage, thus we stained enthesis with col2a1 antibody.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the text.

claim: The col2a1 protein levels are relatively low at P14, and significantly increase after P28.
source: The IHC results show the col2a1 protein levels are relatively low at P14, and significantly increase after P28 (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by IHC images in Figure 1b and quantification in Figure 1c.

claim: After the elimination of doublets, dead, and apoptotic cells, blood cells (erythrocytes and progenitors), endothelial cells, immune cells (B cells and T cells), myeloid cells, and growth plate chondrocytes, high-quality transcriptomic data from 8368 single cells was obtained, including 1285 P1 cells, 4059 P7 cells, 918 P11 cells, 307 P14 cells, 329 P18 cells, 568 P28 cells, and 897 P28 cells.
source: After the elimination of doublets, dead, and apoptotic cells, blood cells (erythrocytes and progenitors), endothelial cells, immune cells (B cells and T cells), myeloid cells, and growth plate chondrocytes, we got high-quality transcriptomic data from 8368 single cells, including 1285 P1 cells, 4059 P7 cells, 918 P11 cells, 307 P14 cells, 329 P18 cells, 568 P28 cells, and 897 P28 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim provides specific quantitative data about the single-cell dataset and references Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: All the cell clusters were annotated, including BTJ chondrocytes, BTJ tendons, Tenocytes, Osteocytes, Enthesoblasts, Tenoblasts, and Mesenchymal progenitors.
source: Based on the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), all the cell clusters were annotated, including BTJ chondrocytes, BTJ tendons, Tenocytes, Osteocytes, Enthesoblasts, Tenoblasts, and Mesenchymal progenitors (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by UMAP visualization in Figure 2b and DEG analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: All cell subtypes achieved high ROGUE values of >0.9, which suggested accuracy in unsupervised cell clustering.
source: We used an entropy-based metric (ROUGE) for assessing the purity of single-cell clusters, all these cell subtypes achieved high ROGUE values of >0.9 (Liu et al., 2020), which suggested accuracy in unsupervised cell clustering (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text, references a method from Liu et al., 2020, and is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Enthesis progenitors had relatively high expression of Ly6a, Cd44, and Pdgfrα, in agreement with progenitors found in tendons and bone marrow.
source: Generally, enthesis progenitors had relatively high expression of Ly6a, Cd44, and Pdgfrα, in agreement with progenitors found in tendons and bone marrow (Harvey et al., 2019; Tikhonova et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Harvey et al., 2019 and Tikhonova et al., 2019.

claim: Enthesoblasts were defined based on their relatively decreased stemness transcriptional signatures, as well as co-expressed tenogenic (e.g. Scx, Col1a1) and chondrogenic markers (e.g. Sox9, Acan).
source: Enthesoblasts were defined based on their relatively decreased stemness transcriptional signatures, as well as co-expressed tenogenic (e.g. Scx, Col1a1) and chondrogenic markers (e.g. Sox9, Acan) (Jensen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Jensen et al., 2018.

claim: Previously reported enthesis marker genes Sox9 and Scx, as well as enthesis-specific ECM genes (Col2a1), were ubiquitously expressed in BTJ chondrocyte cells.
source: We checked the previously reported enthesis marker genes Sox9 and Scx, as well as enthesis-specific ECM genes (Col2a1), which were ubiquitously expressed in BTJ chondrocyte cells (Figure 2e).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by spatial transcriptomic data in Figure 2e.

claim: Sox9+ and Scx+ cells were detected in the enthesis area, mostly in the neonatal stage and significantly decreased in postnatal weeks 2 and 4.
source: We then performed an immunofluorescence assay to validate the spatial distribution of enthesis-related genes, we found that Sox9+ and Scx+ cells were detected in the enthesis area, mostly in the neonatal stage and significantly decreased in postnatal weeks 2 and 4, as expected (Figure 2f).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2f.

claim: The Cytotrace results showed that across all cell clusters, the 'stemness' degree of mesenchymal progenitors is higher than other cell types.
source: The Cytotrace results showed that across all cell clusters, the 'stemness' degree of mesenchymal progenitors is higher than other cell types (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by CytoTRACE analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: CytoTRACE scores of the enthesis cells (BTJ chondrocytes cells) skewed toward a moderate predicted stem potential, which was slightly higher than that in tendon cells, suggestive of a higher degree of stemness for enthesis cells developing into fibrocartilage cells.
source: Among tendon and enthesis-associated cell groups, CytoTRACE scores of the enthesis cells (BTJ chondrocytes cells) skewed toward a moderate predicted stem potential, which was slightly higher than that in tendon cells, suggestive of a higher degree of stemness for enthesis cells developing into fibrocartilage cells (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by CytoTRACE analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The trajectory results showed enthesoblasts originated from mesenchymal progenitors, and enthesoblasts had a greater chance to branch into enthesis chondrocytes.
source: We next implemented RNA velocity analysis. The trajectory results showed enthesoblasts originated from mesenchymal progenitors, and enthesoblasts had a greater chance to branch into enthesis chondrocytes (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Four clusters of cells were predicted as the terminal differentiate clusters: BTJ chondrocytes, tenocytes, and two subsets of osteocytes.
source: Next, we employed developmental potential calculated by Cytotrace to compute the terminal states among all the cell groups by Cellrank, which is a toolkit based on Markov state modeling (Lange et al., 2022), and four clusters of cells were predicted as the terminal differentiate clusters: BTJ chondrocytes, tenocytes, and two subsets of osteocytes (Figure 3d), suggesting that the differentiation profile of these cell groups was separative from each other.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text, references Cellrank method from Lange et al., 2022, and is supported by analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The fate probabilities analysis showed that only BTJ chondrocytes contributed to the fate of enthesis chondrocytes.
source: The fate probabilities analysis showed that only BTJ chondrocytes contributed to the fate of enthesis chondrocytes (Figure 3e and f), which was consistent with RNA velocity, suggesting that the fibrocartilage in postnatal enthesis origin from enthesis site-specific progenitors, instead of tendon cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by fate probability analysis shown in Figures 3e and 3f.

claim: The fibrocartilage in postnatal enthesis origin from enthesis site-specific progenitors, instead of tendon cells.
source: The fate probabilities analysis showed that only BTJ chondrocytes contributed to the fate of enthesis chondrocytes (Figure 3e and f), which was consistent with RNA velocity, suggesting that the fibrocartilage in postnatal enthesis origin from enthesis site-specific progenitors, instead of tendon cells.
evidence: This claim is stated as an inference from the fate probability and RNA velocity analyses shown in Figures 3c, 3e, and 3f.

claim: BTJ chondrocytes correlate slightly with tenocytes, because the genes that correlate positively with the BTJ chondrocyte fate correlate moderately with the tendon fate and vice versa.
source: However, we found BTJ chondrocytes correlate slightly with tenocytes, because the genes that correlate positively with the BTJ chondrocyte fate correlate moderately with the tendon fate and vice versa (Figure 3g).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3g.

claim: The expressions of known differential regulator genes were upregulated significantly higher in enthesis-associated trajectories, such as Scx, Sox9, and Tnmd, which were confirmed indispensable for enthesis formation.
source: We found that the expressions of known differential regulator genes were upregulated significantly higher in enthesis-associated trajectories, such as Scx, Sox9, and Tnmd, which were confirmed indispensable for enthesis formation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene expression dynamics shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Genes related to cartilage ECM (Acan, Scrg1) were upregulated along the pseudotime, and highly expressed until the terminal differentiation state, suggesting the collagen and matrix protein synthesis were predominant in postnatal enthesis growth.
source: We also found genes related to cartilage ECM (Acan, Scrg1) were upregulated along the pseudotime, and highly expressed until the terminal differentiation state, suggesting the collagen and matrix protein synthesis were predominant in postnatal enthesis growth.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene expression dynamics shown in Figure 3h.

claim: Mineralization-related genes (Ibsp, Col11a1) were observed to increase in enthesis chondrocyte differentiation, but less than their expression levels in osteocytes.
source: Meanwhile, mineralization-related genes (Ibsp, Col11a1) were observed to increase in enthesis chondrocyte differentiation, but less than their expression levels in osteocytes (Figure 3h).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene expression dynamics shown in Figure 3h.

claim: The mesenchymal progenitors had the highest differential potential, and the differentiate routine starting from mesenchymal progenitors to enthesoblasts and finally to enthesis chondrocytes.
source: In consistence with the differentiating order predicted by Cytotrace algorithm, the mesenchymal progenitors had the highest differential potential, and the differentiate routine starting from mesenchymal progenitors to enthesoblasts and finally to enthesis chondrocytes (Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by trajectory analysis shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The biological processes alike extracellular matrix organization, collagen fibril organization, and regulation of cellular response to growth factors stimulus were significantly upregulated with enthesis developmental time increasing to postnatal day 14, 28, and 56.
source: The biological processes alike extracellular matrix organization, collagen fibril organization, and regulation of cellular response to growth factors stimulus were significantly upregulated with enthesis developmental time increasing to postnatal day 14, 28, and 56 (Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by time-dependent GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Genes in Module 15 and Module 22 were expressed preferentially in BTJ chondrocytes, which were annotated for cartilage development, ossification, and biomineralization.
source: We found genes in Module 15 and Module 22 were expressed preferentially in BTJ chondrocytes, which were annotated for cartilage development, ossification, and biomineralization (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene module analysis shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Stemness-related genes (Ly6a, Cd34, and Cd44) were downregulated along the trajectories, whose gene modules annotated for mesenchyme morphogenesis, regulation of organ formation, and regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation.
source: In contrast, stemness-related genes (Ly6a, Cd34, and Cd44) were downregulated along the trajectories, whose gene modules annotated for mesenchyme morphogenesis, regulation of organ formation, and regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene module analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of Tnn increased and reached the top at postnatal week 2 (P14), and the expression of Mfge8 increased and maintained a higher level after birth.
source: We found the expression of Mfge8 and Tnn had not been reported, and we validated the expression of Mfge8 and Tnn proteins in enthesis, as the expression of Tnn increased and reached the top at postnatal week 2 (P14), and the expression of Mfge8 increased and maintained a higher level after birth (Figure 4j).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4j.

claim: BTJ chondrocytes were enriched with genes annotated for cartilage development, extracellular matrix organization, and biomineral tissue development.
source: As expected, BTJ chondrocytes were enriched with genes annotated for cartilage development, extracellular matrix organization, and biomineral tissue development, and enthesoblasts were enriched with fibroblast proliferation and developmental growth involved in morphogenesis (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figures 5a and 5b.

claim: Enthesoblasts were enriched with fibroblast proliferation and developmental growth involved in morphogenesis.
source: As expected, BTJ chondrocytes were enriched with genes annotated for cartilage development, extracellular matrix organization, and biomineral tissue development, and enthesoblasts were enriched with fibroblast proliferation and developmental growth involved in morphogenesis (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figures 5a and 5b.

claim: Biological processes alike chondrocyte proliferation, development, and biomineral tissue development decreased with time increased to P56.
source: The time-dependent analysis of each GO annotation in BTJ chondrocytes showed that biological processes alike chondrocyte proliferation, development, and biomineral tissue development decreased with time increased to P56.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by time-dependent GO analysis shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The activity of collagen synthesis maintained a steady level from after birth to postnatal days 28 and 56.
source: While the activity of collagen synthesis maintained a steady level from after birth to postnatal days 28 and 56 (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by time-dependent GO analysis shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Previously reported enthesis-related regulon Sox9 was significantly expressed both in BTJ tenocytes and chondrocytes, in comparison with other cell types.
source: The results showed that previously reported enthesis-related regulon Sox9 was significantly expressed both in BTJ tenocytes and chondrocytes, in comparison with other cell types.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by SCENIC analysis shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Sox9 regulon is mostly expressed in chondrocytes and some parts of tenocytes adjunct to enthesis.
source: We then checked the Sox9 expression in single-cell dataset and spatial transcriptomics, the results showed that Sox9 regulon is mostly expressed in chondrocytes and some parts of tenocytes adjunct to enthesis.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: The downstream targets of Sox9 regulon were mostly genes known associated with cartilage development (Acan, Scrg1, Hapln1, Chad).
source: Target gene analysis showed the downstream targets of Sox9 regulon were mostly genes known associated with cartilage development (Acan, Scrg1, Hapln1, Chad) (Figure 5e).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by target gene analysis shown in Figure 5e.

claim: In an early stage of postnatal growth (P1 and P7), Sox9-positive cells were widely located in the tendon enthesis and humeral head, and the expression of Sox9 decreased with time increased, partly visible in the enthesis cell.
source: In-vivo validation results showed that in an early stage of postnatal growth (P1 and P7), Sox9-positive cells were widely located in the tendon enthesis and humeral head. And the expression of Sox9 decreased with time increased, partly visible in the enthesis cell (Figure 5f).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Mef2a/Mef2c had been reported relative to biomineralization and chondrocyte hypertrophy.
source: In addition, we checked the expression of Mef2a/Mef2c, which had been reported relative to biomineralization and chondrocyte hypertrophy (Chen et al., 2023; Leupin et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Chen et al., 2023 and Leupin et al., 2007.

claim: Mef2a/Mef2c positive populations were found at the SST enthesis, and were more abundant at the mid-stage of enthesis differentiation (P14-P28), consistent with the emergence of fibrochondrocytes observed in histological stainings.
source: Immunofluorescence revealed that these Mef2a/Mef2c positive populations were found at the SST enthesis, and were more abundant at the mid-stage of enthesis differentiation (P14-P28), consistent with the emergence of fibrochondrocytes observed in histological stainings (Figure 5h).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5h.

claim: The cluster of BTJ chondrocytes predominately showed incoming patterns, as suggestive of signaling receivers.
source: We then identified the signaling roles of each subcluster, the results showed that the cluster of BTJ chondrocytes predominately showed incoming patterns, as suggestive of signaling receivers (Figure 6b).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by signaling role analysis shown in Figure 6b.

claim: FGF and BMP signalings are crucial to articular cartilage development.
source: FGF and BMP signalings are crucial to articular cartilage development, yet their specific roles in enthesis development need further investigation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the text.

claim: BTJ chondrocytes, tenocytes, and mesenchymal progenitors were leading senders of FGF signaling.
source: First, the expression pattern of FGF-FGFR signaling was noticed, as both autocrine and paracrine in BTJ chondrocyte. BTJ chondrocytes, tenocytes, and mesenchymal progenitors were leading senders of FGF signaling (Figure 6e).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by FGF signaling network analysis shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Fgfr2 expressed mostly in BTJ chondrocyte cells via Fgf2-Fgfr2 or Fgf9-Fgfr2.
source: We observed Fgfr2 expressed mostly in BTJ chondrocyte cells via Fgf2-Fgfr2 or Fgf9-Fgfr2, and we validated the expression of FGFR2 protein in enthesis by immunofluorescence staining (Figure 6f, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by ligand-receptor analysis and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6f and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) superfamily includes a family of proteins, such as TGF-βs (TGF-β1, TGF-β2, and TGF-β3) and bone morphogenetic proteins (e.g. BMP2, BMP4).
source: The transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) superfamily includes a family of proteins, such as TGF-βs (TGF-β1, TGF-β2, and TGF-β3) and bone morphogenetic proteins (e.g. BMP2, BMP4).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the text.

claim: In the BMP signaling network, the BTJ chondrocytes acted as critical receivers and contributors by secreting BMP ligand Bmpr2.
source: In the BMP signaling network, the BTJ chondrocytes acted as critical receivers and contributors by secreting BMP ligand Bmpr2, especially (Figure 6g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by BMP signaling network analysis shown in Figure 6g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: BMPR2 was observed highly expressed in enthesis from P7 to P56.
source: In immunofluorescence results, BMPR2 was observed highly expressed in enthesis from P7 to P56.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: Ligand-receptor analysis points to Bmp2 and Bmp4 sent from mesenchymal progenitors and enthesoblasts to BTJ chondrocytes, suggesting the important role of BMP signaling in enthesis differentiation.
source: Ligand-receptor analysis points to Bmp2 and Bmp4 sent from mesenchymal progenitors and enthesoblasts to BTJ chondrocytes, suggesting the important role of BMP signaling in enthesis differentiation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by ligand-receptor analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: BTJ chondrocytes majorly received the stimulation by TGF-β1, TGF-β3, and Pthlh, which had been reported positive in chondrocyte differentiation and biomineralization, respectively.
source: In addition, the communication network of TGF-β and PTH signaling pathways was checked, as BTJ chondrocytes majorly received the stimulation by TGF-β1, TGF-β3, and Pthlh, which had been reported positive in chondrocyte differentiation and biomineralization, respectively (Bobzin et al., 2021; Xiao et al., 2022; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Bobzin et al., 2021 and Xiao et al., 2022, as well as signaling network analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The development of fibrocartilage at the enthesis of mouse RC occurs no earlier than 2 weeks after birth.
source: However, the development of fibrocartilage at the enthesis of mouse RC occurs no earlier than 2 weeks after birth (Galatz et al., 2007), suggesting the investigation at the postnatal stage of cellular and genomic mechanisms in enthesis development is needed.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Galatz et al., 2007.

claim: Fang F et al. found enthesis progenitors (Gli1+ progenitors) and validated their stemness in-vitro and in-vivo, within the timepoints from P11 to P56.
source: According to the works performed by Fang F et al., (Fang et al., 2022), they found enthesis progenitors (Gli1+ progenitors) and validated their stemness in-vitro and in-vivo, within the timepoints from P11 to P56.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Fang et al., 2022.

claim: Three distinct populations appear where supraspinatus tendon attaches to the humeral head cartilage: tendon midsubstance progenitors, enthesis progenitors, and primary cartilage progenitors.
source: According to prior studies, three distinct populations appear where supraspinatus tendon attaches to the humeral head cartilage: tendon midsubstance progenitors, enthesis progenitors, and primary cartilage progenitors (Blitz et al., 2013; Dyment et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Blitz et al., 2013 and Dyment et al., 2015.

claim: Enthesis morphogenesis involves predominately enthesis progenitors transforming into fibrocartilage, during which process enthesis progenitors are organized as an unmineralized cartilaginous attachment unit and then mineralizes via endochondral ossification postnatally.
source: Enthesis morphogenesis involves predominately enthesis progenitors transforming into fibrocartilage, during which process enthesis progenitors are organized as an unmineralized cartilaginous attachment unit and then mineralizes via endochondral ossification postnatally (Galatz et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Galatz et al., 2007.

claim: Fibrocartilage did not appear at the BTJ site in mice until 2–3 weeks after birth.
source: We used H&E staining to characterize the morphological changes of the cellular components of enthesis after birth. We found that fibrocartilage did not appear at the BTJ site in mice until 2–3 weeks after birth, and the statistical results showed that enthesis cells' size increased significantly during postnatal development at 7–14 days after birth (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by H&E staining observations shown in Figure 1.

claim: At 14 days after birth, these cells showed a typical chondrocyte phenotype.
source: At 14 days after birth, these cells showed a typical chondrocyte phenotype. This is consistent with the findings of Galatz et al., 2007.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Galatz et al., 2007.

claim: The postnatal 7–14 days were the critical stages for fibrocartilage cell differentiation in enthesis.
source: We consider that the postnatal 7–14 days were the critical stages for fibrocartilage cell differentiation in enthesis, based on the results of our cell morphology studies.
evidence: This claim is stated as an inference based on cell morphology studies.

claim: Schwartz AG et al. reported that Gli1-expressing cells significantly increased and populated at the enthesis site since postnatal day 7, well before the onset of mineralization, and persisted in the mature enthesis.
source: Consistent with the timing we found, Schwartz AG et al., reported that Gli1-expressing cells significantly increased and populated at the enthesis site since postnatal day 7, well before the onset of mineralization, and persisted in the mature enthesis (Schwartz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Schwartz et al., 2015.

claim: Difficulties in restoring the mechanical properties after BTJ injury are largely due to the failure of fibrocartilage recapitulation.
source: It is generally recognized that difficulties in restoring the mechanical properties after BTJ injury are largely due to the failure of fibrocartilage recapitulation (Shengnan et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Shengnan et al., 2021.

claim: In modern RC reconstruction surgeries, anchors fix the tendon to the insertion areas without access to bone marrow, which means BMSCs are not likely the main stem cell source for repair.
source: Moreover, in modern RC reconstruction surgeries, anchors fix the tendon to the insertion areas without access to bone marrow, which means BMSCs are not likely the main stem cell source for repair (Bi et al., 2007; Schwartz et al., 2015; Utsunomiya et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Bi et al., 2007, Schwartz et al., 2015, and Utsunomiya et al., 2013.

claim: Tnn was one of the driving genes in chondrogenic fibroblasts differentiating into fibrochondrocytes.
source: We also noticed that Tnn was one of the driving genes in chondrogenic fibroblasts differentiating into fibrochondrocytes, and we confirmed the existence of the tenascin N protein (also named tenascin W) in the developing fibrocartilage layer.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by driving gene analysis and immunofluorescence validation shown in Figure 4.

claim: Tenascin-W has been reported to be expressed in developing and mature bone, specifically in a subset of stem cell niches.
source: We still know very little about the basic biology of tenascin W, which has been reported to be expressed in developing and mature bone, specifically in a subset of stem cell niches (Meloty-Kapella et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Meloty-Kapella et al., 2006.

claim: The stimulating effects of tenascin-W on osteoblastic progenitors' differentiation and migration have been reported.
source: Details are scarce, but the stimulating effects of tenascin-W on osteoblastic progenitors' differentiation and migration have been reported (Meloty-Kapella et al., 2008; Morgan et al., 2011), suggesting its potential role in facilitating enthesis progenitors differentiating into fibrochondrocytes.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Meloty-Kapella et al., 2008 and Morgan et al., 2011.

claim: Enthesis cells mainly received signals from other cell types, instead of sending signaling factors.
source: We found that enthesis cells mainly received signals from other cell types, instead of sending signaling factors.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by cell-cell interaction analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Pre-hypertrophic cells in the growth plate express high levels of Fgfr3, and hypertrophic chondrocytes express high levels of Fgfr1.
source: According to the literature, pre-hypertrophic cells in the growth plate express high levels of Fgfr3, and hypertrophic chondrocytes express high levels of Fgfr1 (Ornitz and Itoh, 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Ornitz and Itoh, 2015.

claim: Enthesis cells mainly expressed Fgfr2, suggesting that the regulation of FGFs in enthesis progenitors differentiating into fibrocartilage cells was different from growth plate cartilage.
source: Yet we found enthesis cells mainly expressed Fgfr2, suggesting that the regulation of FGFs in enthesis progenitors differentiating into fibrocartilage cells was different from growth plate cartilage.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Enthesis development in the mouse mandible was regulated by FGF signaling via FGFR2-FGF2 signaling.
source: Recent work has confirmed that enthesis development in the mouse mandible was regulated by FGF signaling via FGFR2-FGF2 signaling (Roberts et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Roberts et al., 2019.

claim: One key feature of the Sox9 and Scx positive progenitors is their dependence on Bmp2 and Bmp4 for specification and differentiation.
source: We next noticed the BMP signaling (specifically Bmp2, Bmp4) was expressed in enthesis cells, as one key feature of the Sox9 and Scx positive progenitors is their dependence on Bmp2 and Bmp4 for specification and differentiation (Blitz et al., 2013; Bobzin et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Blitz et al., 2013 and Bobzin et al., 2021.

claim: BMP4 derived from the tendon tip induces enthesis progenitors differentiating into chondrocytes, and conditional inactivation of Bmp4 using Scx-Cre blocks formation of the cartilage anlage prefiguring the bone eminence.
source: Blitz et al., found that BMP4 derived from the tendon tip induces enthesis progenitors differentiating into chondrocytes, and conditional inactivation of Bmp4 using Scx-Cre blocks formation of the cartilage anlage prefiguring the bone eminence (Blitz et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Blitz et al., 2009.

claim: BMP2 could upregulate tenascin-N expression through a p38-dependent signaling pathway.
source: Interestingly, it has been indicated that BMP2 could upregulate tenascin-N expression through a p38-dependent signaling pathway (Scherberich et al., 2005), and we found Tnn was among the top driving genes in fibrochondrocyte differentiation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Scherberich et al., 2005.

claim: TGF-β was important due to its crucial role in cartilage and tendon development.
source: We also found the TGF-β signaling in enthesis cells, as TGF-β was important due to its crucial role in cartilage and tendon development (Killian, 2022).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Killian, 2022.

claim: Canonical TGF-β ligands may be diffuse into the near tendon and enthesis, positive in recruiting chondrogenic cells, and the secretion of TGF-β1 has been confirmed mechanically mediated.
source: Canonical TGF-β ligands may be diffuse into the near tendon and enthesis, positive in recruiting chondrogenic cells, and the secretion of TGF-β1 has been confirmed mechanically mediated (Subramanian et al., 2018; Xiao et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Subramanian et al., 2018 and Xiao et al., 2022.
